items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: That's about the only time I recorded with him, yeah.

ctx.x: Because he wouldn't have been there with Russell.

No. Well, he could have been with Morton. I guess all the rest of the fellows that were there that wasn't with Russell was with Jelly Roll. But there was a gang of them in there. I can't remember all of them. In fact, there's very few of them I can remember. Right now I can't think of nobody's name.
But you recognized your own playing on one of the records.

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: I don't know how to even start that, because I don't know what happened. Russell was supposed to get a group to record with Wilton Crawley, and Jelly Roll was supposed to play piano. And Jelly Roll walked in there with his group... So I don't know, we compromised. Some of the guys played some of the

ctx.x: ...they'd egg him on and tell him 'You can't play piano' and...

Oh yeah, he would talk... Oh, he loved to play. Play and sing his numbers. Sure. Jelly was all right if you knew him. Yeah, Jelly Roll contributed a lot to music. Good guy. No dummy. He was not a dummy at all.
Now, you recorded with him at one time.

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: After that, I met him, you know, and I found out who he was.

ctx.x: And where did you first run into Jelly Roll Morton? Was it at the Rhythm Club?

No, it was the Bandbox. He come in the Bandbox, and he was playing piano in there. Somebody said to me, 'That's Jelly Roll Morton.' I said, 'Jelly Morton? I never heard of him.' He was sittin' down there playin' the piano, Mister Jelly Lord. Mister Jelly Lord! I don't know what the hell can I say about him. Mister'Jelly Lord, don't come up with that old-time stuff! Heh-heh. After that, I met him, you know, and I found out who he was. He was all right. But he'd stand out on the corner and give all the musicians…
